title: “I Love You” by People!
text: "I Love You" is a 1965 song by the Zombies, written by their bassist Chris White. Written during a tour of France, the song was written at a time the Zombies' mainstream popularity was slowly fading.

title: “Take Time to Know Her” by Percy Sledge
text: "Take Time to Know Her" is a song written by Steve Davis and performed by Percy Sledge. It reached #5 on the Canadian pop chart, #6 on the U.S. R&B chart, and #11 on the U.S. pop chart in 1968.
listen: Take Time to Know Her Percy Sledge

title: “Pictures of Matchstick Men” by Status Quo
text: "Pictures of Matchstick Men" is the first hit single by British rock band the Status Quo. It was released on 5 January 1968.
listen: Pictures of Matchstick Men Status Quo

title: “Summertime Blues” by Blue Cheer
text: "Summertime Blues" is a song co-written and recorded by the American rock artist Eddie Cochran. It was written by Cochran and his manager Jerry Capehart.

title: “Ain't Nothing Like the Real Thing” by Marvin Gaye & Tammi Terrell
text: "Ain't Nothing Like the Real Thing" is a single released by American R&B/soul duo Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell, on the Tamla label in 1968. The B-side of the single is "Little Ole Boy, Little Ole Girl" from the duo's United LP. The first release off the duo's second album: You're All I Need, the song—written and produced by regular Gaye/Terrell collaborators Ashford & Simpson—became a hit within weeks of release …

title: “I Got the Feelin'” by James Brown
text: "I Got the Feelin'" is a funk song by James Brown. Released as a single in 1968, it reached No.
listen: I Got the Feelin' James Brown

title: “I've Gotta Get a Message to You” by The Bee Gees
text: "I've Gotta Get a Message to You" is a song by the Bee Gees. Released as a single in 1968, it was their second number-one hit in the UK Singles Chart, and their first US Top 10 hit.
wiki: I've Gotta Get a Message to You
listen: I've Gotta Get a Message to You The Bee Gees

title: “Lady Madonna” by The Beatles
text: "Lady Madonna" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles, written primarily by Paul McCartney and credited to Lennon–McCartney. In March 1968, it was released as a mono non-album single backed with "The Inner Light".

title: “Hurdy Gurdy Man” by Donovan
text: "Hurdy Gurdy Man" is a song by Scottish singer-songwriter Donovan. It was recorded in April 1968 and released the following month as a single.

title: “Magic Carpet Ride” by Steppenwolf
text: "Magic Carpet Ride" is a rock song written by John Kay and Rushton Moreve from the Canadian-American hard rock band Steppenwolf. The song was initially released in 1968 on the album The Second.

title: “Bottle of Wine” by The Fireballs
text: "Bottle of Wine" is a song written and recorded by Tom Paxton in 1965, and covered by The Fireballs in 1967. Their version peaked at #9 on the Billboard Hot 100 in March 1968 and #5 in Canada.

title: “Stay in My Corner” by The Dells
text: "Stay in My Corner" is a 1965 soul song by The Dells. It was released as a single on the Vee-Jay label and peaked in the top 30 on the R&B singles chart.
listen: Stay in My Corner The Dells

title: “Soul Serenade” by Willie Mitchell
text: "Soul Serenade" is a jazz instrumental written by King Curtis and Luther Dixon. Curtis played the lead on a B-flat saxello, a version of the soprano sax.

title: “Delilah” by Tom Jones
text: "Delilah" is a song recorded by Welsh singer Tom Jones in December 1967. The lyrics were written by Barry Mason, and the music by Les Reed, who also contributed the title and theme of the song.

title: “Nobody but Me” by The Human Beinz
text: "Nobody but Me" is a song written by O'Kelly, Rudolph, and Ronald Isley of The Isley Brothers and first recorded by The Isley Brothers in 1962. The most commercially successful and widely known version to date is the 1968 US Top 10 hit by The Human Beinz, which was their only major chart success.
listen: Nobody but Me The Human Beinz

title: “I Thank You” by Sam & Dave
text: "I Thank You" is a song written by David Porter and Isaac Hayes originally recorded by Sam & Dave, released in early 1968. The single was Sam & Dave's final release on Stax Records, reaching No.

title: “The Fool on the Hill” by Sérgio Mendes & Brasil '66
text: "The Fool on the Hill" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles from their 1967 EP and album Magical Mystery Tour. It was written and sung by Paul McCartney and credited to the Lennon–McCartney partnership.
listen: The Fool on the Hill Sérgio Mendes & Brasil '66

title: “Sky Pilot” by The Animals
text: "Sky Pilot" is a 1968 song by Eric Burdon & the Animals, released on the album The Twain Shall Meet. When released as a single the song was split across both sides, due to its length.

title: “Indian Lake” by The Cowsills
text: "Indian Lake" is a song with music and lyrics written by Tony Romeo. It was recorded by the pop band The Cowsills, and included on their 1968 album Captain Sad and His Ship of Fools.

title: “I Wonder What She's Doing Tonight” by Tommy Boyce & Bobby Hart
text: "I Wonder What She's Doing Tonight" is a song written and originally recorded by Tommy Boyce and Bobby Hart. The Boyce and Hart composition was arranged by Artie Butler.
wiki: I Wonder What She's Doing Tonight
listen: I Wonder What She's Doing Tonight Tommy Boyce & Bobby Hart

title: “Over You” by Gary Puckett & The Union Gap
text: "Over You" is a song written and composed by Jerry Fuller and recorded by Gary Puckett & The Union Gap for their 1968 album, Incredible.
wiki: Over You (Gary Puckett & The Union Gap song)
listen: Over You Gary Puckett & The Union Gap

title: “Goin' Out of My Head/Can't Take My Eyes Off You” by The Lettermen
text: "Goin' Out of My Head" is a song written by Teddy Randazzo and Bobby Weinstein, initially recorded by Little Anthony and the Imperials in 1964. Randazzo, a childhood friend of the group, wrote the song especially for them, having also supplied the group with their previous Top 20 Hit "I'm on the Outside".
listen: Goin' Out of My Head/Can't Take My Eyes Off You The Lettermen

title: “Shoo-Be-Doo-Be-Doo-Da-Day” by Stevie Wonder
text: "Shoo-Be-Doo-Be-Doo-Da-Day" is a 1968 single released by American and Motown recording artist Stevie Wonder. The song, co-written by Wonder and produced by Henry Cosby and Sylvia Moy, was the first to showcase Wonder's talents at the clavinet and was one of his first successful co-written tracks during his 1960s Motown period.

title: “The Unicorn” by The Irish Rovers
text: "The Unicorn" is a song written by Shel Silverstein. It was originally released in 1962 on his album Inside Folk Songs.

title: “You Keep Me Hangin' On” by Vanilla Fudge
text: "You Keep Me Hangin' On" is a song written and composed by Holland–Dozier–Holland. It was first recorded in 1966 by American Motown group the Supremes, reaching number one on the Billboard Hot 100.
listen: You Keep Me Hangin' On Vanilla Fudge

title: “Revolution” by The Beatles
text: "Revolution" is a song by the English rock band the Beatles, written by John Lennon and credited to the Lennon–McCartney partnership. title: “Woman, Woman” by Gary Puckett & The Union Gap
text: "Woman, Woman" is the debut single by Gary Puckett & The Union Gap, from their 1968 debut album Woman, Woman. It was written and composed by Jim Glaser and Jimmy Payne, and uses session musicians from The Wrecking Crew.
listen: Woman, Woman Gary Puckett & The Union Gap

title: “Elenore” by The Turtles
text: "Elenore" is a 1968 song by the Turtles, originally included on The Turtles Present the Battle of the Bands. Although written by Howard Kaylan, its writing was co-credited to all five members of the band: Kaylan, Mark Volman, Al Nichol, Jim Pons, and John Barbata.

title: Bombs explode at midnight in two department stores in Frankfurt-am-Main; Andreas Baader and Gudrun Ensslin are later arrested and sentenced for arson.
text: Gudrun Ensslin was a German far-left terrorist and founder of the West German far-left militant group Red Army Faction (Rote Armee Fraktion, or RAF, also known as the Baader-Meinhof Gang). After becoming involved with co-founder Andreas Baader, Ensslin was influential in the development of his political beliefs.

title: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.: Martin Luther King Jr. is shot dead at the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, Tennessee by James Earl Ray. King-assassination riots erupt in major American cities, lasting for several days afterwards.
text: Martin Luther King Jr. was an American civil rights activist and Baptist minister who was a prominent leader of the civil rights movement from 1955 until his assassination in 1968.

title: Apollo program: Apollo-Saturn mission 502 (Apollo 6) is launched, as the second and last uncrewed test-flight of the Saturn V launch vehicle.
text: Apollo 6, also known as AS-502, was the third and final uncrewed flight in the United States' Apollo program and the second test of the Saturn V launch vehicle. The Saturn V's utilization during the mission qualified it for use during human spaceflight, and it was used beginning on Apollo 8 in December 1968.

title: AEK Athens wins the FIBA European Cup Winners Cup Final in basketball against Slavia Prague, in front of a record attendance of 80,000 spectators. It is the first major European trophy won at club level of any sport in Greece.
text: The 1967–68 FIBA European Cup Winners' Cup was the second edition of FIBA's 2nd-tier level European-wide professional club basketball competition, contested between national domestic cup champions, running from November 1967, to 4 April 1968. 22 teams took part in the competition, three more than in the inaugural edition.

title: 13th Eurovision Song Contest is held in the Royal Albert Hall, London, UK. The winning song, Spain's "La, la, la" (music and lyrics by Manuel de la Calva and Ramón Arcusa) is sung in Spanish by Massiel after Spanish authorities refuse to…
text: The Royal Albert Hall is a concert hall on the northern edge of South Kensington, London, England. It has a seating capacity of 5,272.
